name: Juuku Hot Springs
near: Saruu (where the Juuku gorge meets the Balykchy — Karakol highway) and Darkhan; it is ~10–12 km up the valley from the highway to the springs. TripAdvisor lists the site as “Radon Springs Djuuku, Saruu”. The earlier reference to Jalgyz-Uryuk (14.7 km per OSM) is formally the nearest marker in the export, but the real approach goes through Saruu.
elev: 2236 m — per the Destination Jeti Oguz / Nomad's Land catalog (2024–2025). There is no independent measurement; an error of ±50 m is possible.
short: Radon-hydrogen sulfide warm springs (~34 °C) in the side valley of Juukuchak in the Juuku gorge on the southern shore of Issyk-Kul; simple concrete pools in the open air and in a “yurt”, entry 100–150 som.
desc: The springs are on the right side of the Juukuchak valley — a side tributary of the Juuku River, the longest gorge in the Terskey Ala-Too (40–50 km), along which in ancient times ran the route from the Issyk-Kul basin to the Inner Tian Shan and China. The water is thermal (about 34 °C regardless of the weather), mineralized, with radon and a noticeable smell of hydrogen sulfide; several small pools are set up, one of them covered by a concrete “yurt”. The infrastructure is simple, in places neglected — this is not a sanatorium but a village bathing spot. Nearby are a cold mountain river for contrast bathing, the “300 Sheep” cave, red cliffs at the gorge entrance and Tian Shan spruce higher up the valley. In 1932 the Swiss traveler Ella Maillart (“Turkestan Solo”) passed through the valley. Tourists often get confused: the hot springs are in Juukuchak, while the Juuku gorge itself is known for its lakes and the pass to the Arabel plateau.
guide: Come here not for a spa but for the atmosphere: warm water smelling of sulfur, red cliffs and spruces all around, and above — one of the wildest gorges of the Terskey. When ordering a car in Karakol or Saruu, say specifically “Juukuchak, hot springs” — otherwise you risk ending up in the neighbouring valley with no pools. Don't stay in the water for more than 30 minutes: locals themselves warn about the natural radioactivity. After bathing, dip into the icy river nearby and look into the “300 Sheep” cave. If you have a 4×4 / SUV and a spare day, continue up the Juuku to the lakes and the pass to the syrts (high plateaus) of Arabel, along the old caravan route.
see: Warm pools (34 °C) in the open air and in a concrete “yurt”; the cold Juukuchak River for contrast; the “300 Sheep” cave; red sandstone cliffs at the entrance to the Juuku gorge; higher up — spruce forests, a waterfall, the Kashka-Suu (3600 m) and Juukuchak lakes; petroglyphs and Turkic burial mounds in the valley.
skip: You expect a well-equipped spa complex — here there are simple concrete tubs and minimal service. You are without a 4×4 / SUV and not ready for a dirt road with fords. You have already been to Altyn-Arashan or Ak-Suu/Kerege-Tash — the water is similar, and the road there is easier.
diff: Easy on site (a bathing spot by the road); the difficulty is in the approach: 10–12 km of dirt road/off-road from the highway, TripAdvisor (2016–2025) recommends 4WD, mud and fords in spring.
when: May–October for driving the valley; the water is 34 °C year-round, in winter the approach depends on snow and is not guaranteed. In the shoulder season (April–May) the dirt road turns to mud (TripAdvisor reviews).
hours: Google Maps (viewed 03.10.2026): open 24 hours. In practice — a village bathing spot with a caretaker on site; per TripAdvisor reviews the owners opened up outside “hours” too. There is no schedule.
daytime: Daytime or early evening: warm water is nicer in cool weather, but it is better to drive back along the dirt road in daylight.
how: From Karakol (45–75 km) or Bishkek along the southern Balykchy — Karakol highway to the village of Saruu (or Darkhan), then south along the Juuku valley ~10 km to a fork and up the side valley of Juukuchak to the pools. Public transport: marshrutka (minibus) Karakol — Darkhan 70–100 som (Visit Karakol), then ~2 hours on foot or hitchhiking; a taxi/4×4 / SUV is more convenient. When ordering a car, say specifically “Juukuchak, hot springs”.
needcar: Yes. It is 10–12 km from the highway with no public transport; a 4×4 / SUV is advisable (TripAdvisor reviews, too.kg: the road is good at the bottom, worse higher up).
self: Yes, by 4×4 / SUV or on foot from Darkhan/Saruu; no permit needed (not a border zone). Navigation: the Google marker “Juuku istochnik”, maps.me.
roadtype: Paved road along the highway to Saruu; then a dirt road along the valley, “quite good” at first, higher up — broken up, with fords (too.kg; TripAdvisor reviews 2016–2025: “4WD needed”, “a test for jeepers”). To the pools — a dirt road.
traveltime: From Karakol by car ~1.5–2 h (TripAdvisor review 2024: “a couple of hours from Karakol”); from Darkhan on foot ~2 h (Visit Karakol). From Bishkek ~5–6 h to the area.
stay: There is no lodging at the springs themselves (too.kg: no guesthouses, shops or cafes in the gorge; many places for tents). The nearest guesthouses are in Saruu, Darkhan, Kyzyl-Suu and Karakol; CBT Karakol and visitkarakol.com. Specific prices not found.
net: There is no mobile signal in the Juuku gorge (too.kg). By the highway (Saruu) all operators have a signal. Beeline and MegaCom strengthened their network around Issyk-Kul in 2024–2026, but Juuku is not mentioned in the lists.
entry: 100 som per person (Destination Jeti Oguz / Nomad's Land, catalog 2024–2025); issykkul.biz — 100–150 som. Pay on site in cash. Confirm the amount before your visit.
transfer: Marshrutka (minibus) Karakol — Darkhan 70–100 som (visitkarakol.com). An excursion from Cholpon-Ata $417/group, 12 h (sputnik8, 2026). No published taxi tariff to the springs; a guide figure for a 4×4 / SUV from Karakol on comparable myway.kg routes — 9,500–13,200 som per car (2026, “the price is not final due to the fuel shortage”).
bring: Swimwear, a towel, flip-flops, water and food (no shops), cash in som, warm clothes (2200 m, cold in the evening), an offline map; for a 4×4 / SUV — a reserve of fuel.
warn: Water with natural radon: no more than 30 minutes in the pool (Destination Jeti Oguz recommendation); people with cardiovascular diseases and pregnant women should consult a doctor; advertised “healing” promises are not medical advice. The road through the gorge is dirt with fords, dangerous in spring; no mobile signal. Don't confuse it with the Juuku gorge without pools.
food: There is no cafe on site. Bring food with you; in the villages of Saruu/Darkhan and Kyzyl-Suu — ashkana (small eateries) with lagman, manty and kumis (seasonal). Specific places were not checked.
reviews: Google Maps “Juuku istochnik”: 4.7/5, 26 ratings (03.10.2026). TripAdvisor “Juuku Gorge”: 4.5/5, 15 reviews (2016–2025) — they praise the wild nature, the quiet, the marmots; cons — off-road, fords, 4WD needed. TripAdvisor “Radon Springs Djuuku, Saruu”: 10 reviews (2014–2018) — the water is “mineral, slightly sulfurous”, but the facilities are “simple and neglected”.
p.sum: The best option is a car with a driver from Karakol (1.5–2 h) or your own car with good ground clearance: along the southern highway to Saruu, then ~10–12 km of dirt road up the Juuku valley and into the side valley of Juukuchak to the pools (Google marker “Juuku istochnik”, 42.1818, 78.0073). Without a car — a marshrutka (minibus) Karakol — Darkhan/Saruu and ~2 h on foot. There is no lodging, shops, cafes or mobile signal in the gorge: bring food, water and cash, and overnight in a tent by the river or in guesthouses in Kyzyl-Suu/Saruu. Entry to the bathing spot is 100 som, no more than 30 minutes in the water.

p.iti.0.title: A day from Karakol
p.iti.0.plan: 8:00 set out by 4×4 / SUV → 9:30 Saruu, the red cliffs at the entrance → 10:00–11:30 the Juukuchak pools (30 min in the water) + the “300 Sheep” cave → a picnic by the river → a walk up the Juuku to the spruce forests → 16:00 back to Karakol in daylight.
p.iti.1.title: 2 days with a tent
p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: Karakol → springs, bathing, overnight in a tent higher up the Juuku. Day 2: an out-and-back to the waterfall/lakes, an evening visit to the pools, return.
p.iti.2.title: A southern-shore combination
p.iti.2.plan: Karakol → Jeti-Oguz and Kok-Zhaiyk (the Maiden's Tears waterfall) → Juuku (overnight) → Barskoon and the Arabel plateau → Skazka (Fairy Tale) Canyon → Bokonbaevo (Manjyly-Ata, Shatyly).
p.season: May — driving is questionable (mud, water at the fords); June–July — the fords are higher; August–September — the best time (dry, lower water in the rivers); October — cold, but bathing at 34 °C is pleasant; November–April — the approach in snow is not guaranteed. No crowds; ticks in the spruce forests May–June (for the region).
p.budget.economy: Marshrutka (minibus) Bishkek — southern shore 500–600 + Karakol — Darkhan 70–100 som, 2 h on foot; entry 100; a tent free or a guesthouse in Kyzyl-Suu ~$19 (~1,650 som) with breakfast; your own food ~500. In total ~1,500–2,500 som/person for 1–2 days not counting the trip from Bishkek.
p.budget.comfort: A 4×4 / SUV with a driver from Karakol ~9,500–13,200 som/car (MYWAY guide figure) — split among 3–4 people ≈2,500–4,000; entry 100; a night in Karakol $40–60; food 1,000–1,500. In total ~6,000–9,000 som/person.
p.permits: Not needed: not a border zone. Only payment for the bathing spot (100 som) on site in cash.
p.access: With children — possible in the dry season (short bathing, radon); older people — a rough ride on the dirt road, people with cardiovascular diseases should consult a doctor; with a stroller — no (dirt, concrete steps); with a dog — possible, but there are shepherd dogs around.
